Chapter 7: Overcoming Self-Doubt and the Fear of Visibility
As your message starts reaching more people, it’s totally normal to feel a little self-doubt—or even some anxiety—about stepping into the spotlight. You’re not alone; just about everyone who begins sharing their expertise publicly runs into these feelings. Maybe you worry about being criticized, rejected, or feeling like you’re just not enough. If those thoughts ever leave you feeling stuck, you’re definitely not the only one.
Here’s something to pay attention to: self-doubt isn’t a sign of weakness. In fact, it’s usually a sign that you’re growing. It means you actually care about the work you’re doing and how it affects others. So, instead of trying to get rid of the fear, what if you focused on building courage? Courage doesn’t mean you’re never afraid—it’s about moving forward even when things feel uncertain.
Think of your inner critic like a well-meaning, but super overprotective friend. Their job? To keep you safe. But sometimes, that voice ends up holding you back from some awesome opportunities to grow. By noticing when it pops up, and gently questioning what it’s saying, you can start moving forward with more confidence.
Let’s talk about some simple ways you can manage self-doubt:
First, try reframing those negative thoughts. If you ever catch yourself thinking, “Who am I to do this?”—flip it around. Ask yourself, “Who am I not to help, if I can?”
Next, shift your focus away from yourself and toward the people who genuinely need your message. That simple shift can make a huge difference.
Don’t forget to celebrate small wins. Whether it’s a kind note, a positive comment, or even a tiny moment of impact—write it down. Keep a list. Those reminders matter.
And finally, seek support. Reach out to peers, mentors, or communities who really get what you’re going through. Sometimes, just hearing “me too” can make the journey a whole lot easier.
Remember, visibility is a skill—just like anything else. You don’t have to start on a big stage. Practice by sharing your message in low-pressure settings. Maybe it’s chatting with friends, a small group, or posting your thoughts online. As your comfort grows, you can slowly expand to bigger audiences or new platforms. Each step you take builds resilience, and helps remind you why you started in the first place.
Every expert started out as a beginner. The real magic happens when you’re willing to be seen—imperfectly and authentically. That’s what inspires others to step forward, too. When you show up with a little vulnerability and a lot of courage, you give everyone around you permission to grow right alongside you.
